column2: Given these definitions: (1) One is among what God made, and one can turn toward oneself as a whole, as both what God made and what one has made of it, though not every part of oneself can be seen. (2) Facing God's creation can mean facing what God made for what it is, or facing it also as God's work; only the second faces it as creation. (3) Repentance is the turning toward the grace that freely gives a maker the standing toward his own work. Then repentance can turn toward God's creation as God's work, and toward oneself within it as a whole, though not every part of oneself can be seen.
